stories.title: This AI actually learns how your eyes read—what happens next is stunning
stories.source: Futura, le média qui explore le monde
stories.simple_summary: Someone created an AI system that can understand how your eyes move while you read. The headline suggests something surprising will happen next, but the details aren't clear from this title alone.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to engineers and researchers right now — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Flock CEO calls for ‘compromise’ as surveillance company faces growing backlash
stories.simple_summary: Flock Safety is a company that sells camera systems to track vehicles. Many people are worried these cameras could be misused to spy on them, and the company is facing complaints.
stories.why_it_matters: If you live in an area with Flock cameras, know that privacy concerns exist, but this is mainly a debate for communities and lawmakers to settle.

stories.title: ‘We are hitting a different chapter’: OpenAI leader warns of threat of ‘persistent’ AI cyber-attacks
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI's leader is warning that AI systems are becoming targets for hackers who launch repeated attacks to break into them.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to tech companies and investors — it's not an immediate concern for your daily life.

stories.title: Is it legal to train AI models on copyrighted books? It’s complicated
stories.simple_summary: AI companies have used millions of copyrighted books to train their systems without asking authors for permission. Authors are now questioning whether this is legal.
stories.why_it_matters: If you write, create content, or care about supporting artists, this matters — it's a real legal and fairness question being worked out in courts.

stories.title: How Big Tech Captured American Schools
stories.simple_summary: Large tech companies have heavily influenced what gets taught in American schools and how schools operate.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have grandchildren in school or care about education, it's worth paying attention to what technology companies are promoting to students.

stories.title: Alibaba launches $10 billion Hong Kong share placement to fund AI spending
stories.simple_summary: Alibaba, a huge Chinese company, is raising $10 billion to spend on AI technology.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and big business — it's a corporate finance move, not something affecting everyday people.

stories.title: A free AI model is winning over developers. And nobody knows whose servers it runs on
stories.simple_summary: A free AI tool that programmers love to use is popular, but nobody can figure out whose computers actually run it in the background.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly interesting to tech workers — it highlights that sometimes people use tools without fully understanding who's behind them.

stories.title: Harvard’s $699 startup bootcamp offers AI avatars of its instructors
stories.simple_summary: Harvard's business school created an AI teacher — a digital avatar that looks like a real instructor and gives feedback to students practicing their business pitches.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're considering expensive business education, know that some programs now use AI instructors, which might change what you're paying for.

stories.title: Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller Just Sold Some Sandisk Stock and Bought These 3 Unstoppable Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks
stories.simple_summary: A wealthy investor moved money from one tech stock to buy shares in three different AI-related companies.
stories.why_it_matters: This is purely about investment choices — nothing for a regular person or small business owner to act on.

stories.title: Nvidia customers reportedly warned about AI-related price hikes
stories.simple_summary: Nvidia is a company that makes computer chips for AI. Customers are being told that prices for these chips will go up.
stories.why_it_matters: If your small business uses AI tools, prices might slowly increase over time, but this is mainly a concern for tech companies buying expensive equipment.

stories.title: Inherent, founded by DeepMind alumni, says its AI ‘teammate’ just outperformed Anthropic and OpenAI at replicating research
stories.simple_summary: A new AI lab created an AI system that can read and recreate scientific research papers as well as or better than similar tools from bigger companies.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to researchers and scientists — it shows competition in the AI industry, but doesn't affect your daily life.

stories.title: OpenAI says California should strengthen its AI safety bill
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI (the ChatGPT company) is now asking California to make its AI safety rules stronger, even though they opposed similar rules before.
stories.why_it_matters: This is interesting as a sign that even AI companies want government rules — it suggests big tech agrees rules are needed, though what those rules should be is still being decided.
